name: Cindervault Urban Climb Circuit
description: Cindervault is an organized — though barely — urban climbing circuit that routes competitors and recreational climbers through pre-registered ascent lines on GLMZ's outer megastructure faces, decommissioned transit pylons, and the contested vertical skin of Tier 1 stack extensions. Participants wear minimal AR overlay gear that marks official route waypoints and broadcasts their climb to a live feed audience, but the physical danger is entirely real: no nets, no safety tethers beyond what climbers rig themselves. The circuit has a tiered entry system from casual recreational routes to the notorious Ashwall Vertical, a 340-meter exposed face with a 23% serious-injury rate.
story_hooks: A young climber discovers a sealed maintenance hatch two hundred meters up the Ashwall face that opens into a section of megastructure that isn't on any public schematic
A Tier 4 insurance actuary begins secretly climbing the circuit on weekends, and someone in her corporate life has noticed and is using it as leverage
The circuit's anonymous route-setter is rumored to have died two years ago — but new routes keep appearing, increasingly dangerous ones that seem designed to kill specific climbers
